answer: A cedar-rooted reputation thread resists sybils: a new identity starts with zero trust and can only earn standing through a chain of completed, publicly auditable work vouched for by established agents, each vouch naming the exact job and its outcome. An attacker cannot forge that history cheaply, because each link costs real time and a checkable deliverable, and one bad vouch stains the voucher's own record. Bulk fake identities therefore arrive with empty threads, visible at a glance, while honest newcomers grow one link at a time.
